urgency.title: Threats or a rush
urgency.explanation: Scammers threaten arrest, deportation or a closed account so you act before you think.

payment.title: Strange way to pay
payment.explanation: Real agencies never ask for gift cards, crypto, wire transfers, Zelle or Western Union.

government.title: Says it's the government
government.explanation: USCIS, IRS, SSA, ICE and police do not call or text to demand money.

guarantee.title: "Guaranteed" visa or job
guarantee.explanation: No one can guarantee a visa, green card or job abroad — only the government decides.

upfront_fee.title: Pay first
upfront_fee.explanation: Asking for a fee before you receive anything is a classic scam trick.

secrecy.title: Keep it secret
secrecy.explanation: Being told not to tell anyone is a sign someone wants to stop you from getting help.

notario.title: Notario or consultant
notario.explanation: In the US, a notario cannot give legal advice or file immigration cases for you.

prize.title: Prize or lottery
prize.explanation: You can't win a contest you never entered, and real prizes don't cost money.

link.title: Suspicious link
link.explanation: Links in surprise messages often lead to fake sites that steal money or passwords.

low: If it asks for money or documents later, check again before acting.
Contact the person or company using a number you already know.
medium: Don't pay and don't share personal information yet.
Contact the agency or company yourself using the official website below.
Talk to a family member you trust before doing anything.
high: Do not pay — especially not with gift cards, crypto, wire or Zelle.
Do not reply, call back, or click any link in the message.
Contact the real agency using the official website below.
Warn your family so they don't fall for it.

verify.title: Who are you dealing with?
verify.intro: Pick the kind of person or business. We'll show you how to check them with official sources before you pay or share documents.

consultant.label: Immigration consultant or notario
steps: Search their name in the California Secretary of State's immigration consultant list. Consultants must be registered and bonded.
A consultant may only fill in forms you choose and translate. They cannot give legal advice or pick forms for you. A "notario" is not a lawyer in the U.S.
For legal advice, use a licensed lawyer or a DOJ-accredited representative. Get a written contract and receipt, and keep your original documents.

lawyer.label: Lawyer
steps: Look up their name or bar number on the State Bar of California website. Their status should say "Active".
Check for any discipline listed on their State Bar profile. For immigration cases, DOJ-accredited representatives are also allowed.
Ask for a written fee agreement before paying, and always get a receipt.

travel_agent.label: Travel, visa or job-abroad agent
steps: Only U.S. embassies, consulates and USCIS decide visas. No agent can guarantee one.
Real employers don't charge you to get a job. Be careful of anyone asking for fees for a job or visa abroad.
Never pay with cash, gift cards, wire transfer or crypto. Ask a trusted family member before paying anything.

government.label: Someone who says they're from the government
steps: Hang up or don't reply. USCIS, IRS, SSA, ICE and police do not demand gift cards, crypto or wire transfers, or threaten instant arrest.
Call the agency yourself using the number on its official .gov website. Never use the number the caller gave you.
Report it: IRS impersonation to TIGTA, Social Security impersonation to SSA, and everything else to the FTC.

contractor.label: Contractor or home repair
steps: Check their license number on the CSLB website. Make sure the name and status match.
In California, the down payment for home improvement can't be more than $1,000 or 10% of the price, whichever is less.
Get a written contract. Don't pay in cash and don't pay in full before the work is done.

seller.label: Online seller
steps: Search the seller's name with the word "scam" and read reviews. Be careful if the price is much lower than everywhere else.
Pay with a credit card, which lets you dispute a charge. Never pay strangers with gift cards, wire, crypto or Zelle.
If you paid and nothing arrived, call your bank right away, then report it to the FTC.

learn.title: Learn the common scams
learn.intro: These are scams families in our area really receive. This page also works without internet once you've opened it.

uscis_call.title: Fake USCIS call
uscis_call.example: "This is USCIS. There's a problem with your file. Pay a fine today or you will be deported."
signs: Wants payment by phone, gift card or wire
The caller ID can be faked to look like USCIS
uscis_call.action: Hang up. USCIS never asks for payment by phone. Log in to your USCIS account or call 800-375-5283 yourself.

notario.title: Notario fraud
notario.example: "I'm a notario. I can get your papers fast, no lawyer needed."
signs: Calls themselves a notario or immigration expert
Keeps your original documents or asks you to sign blank forms
notario.action: Only a licensed lawyer or DOJ-accredited representative can give immigration legal advice. Check them first.

visa_agent.title: Fake visa or job-abroad agent
visa_agent.example: "Canada or USA visa 100% guaranteed! Send the fee first. Seats are limited."
visa_agent.action: No one can guarantee a visa. Don't pay. Ask a trusted family member and check with official sources.

irs_ssa.title: IRS or Social Security threat
irs_ssa.example: "Your Social Security number is suspended. A warrant will be issued unless you pay now."
signs: Asks for gift cards, crypto or wire
irs_ssa.action: Hang up. The IRS and SSA contact you by mail first and never demand gift cards. Call them yourself from the official website.

grandparent.title: Grandchild or family emergency call
grandparent.example: "Grandma, it's me. I'm in jail. Please send money and don't tell Mom and Dad."
signs: A crying or rushed voice saying it's a relative
Asks you to keep it secret
Needs money right now by gift card, cash or wire
grandparent.action: Hang up and call your family member on the number you already have. Ask a question only they would know.

toll_package.title: Fake toll or package text
toll_package.example: "FasTrak: you have an unpaid toll of $4.15. Pay now to avoid a penalty: (link)"
signs: Small amount with a strange link
Threat of a late fee or penalty
You weren't expecting a package or toll bill
toll_package.action: Don't click the link. Check your account on the official website or app you already use, then delete the text.
